subject: FRE
label: Grade 04
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 04 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Reading short texts
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Reading short texts', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read and answer. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Reading short texts' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and answer, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Texte: 'Une eleve habite a Lyon. Elle a douze ans. Elle aime lire.' Ou habite l'eleve? A Lyon. A toi d'ecrire: 'Je m'appelle... J'habite a... J'aime...' Method: Model run for 'Reading short texts'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read and answer: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Read the whole text once for the general idea. Je m'appelle Nora. J'ai neuf ans. J'habite à Lyon avec ma mère, mon père et mon chat. Le matin, je vais à l'école à pied. J'aime lire et dessiner. Le mercredi, je joue au tennis. Ask: who is speaking, and about what? [Nora, about herself.]

Step 2, Work out the meaning line by line. J'habite [I live], avec ma mère [with my mother], le matin [in the morning], à pied [on foot], j'aime lire [I like reading], le mercredi [on Wednesdays]. Underline words that look like English, such as tennis, and words you already know, such as chat and école.

Step 3, Learn the question words. Qui ? [Who?] Où ? [Where?] Quand ? [When?] Quel âge ? [How old?] Que fait-elle ? [What does she do?] Match: Où habite Nora ? Look for habite in the text, then answer: Elle habite à Lyon. [She lives in Lyon.]

Step 4, Answer in a full sentence. Quel âge a Nora ? [How old is Nora?] Nora a neuf ans. [Nora is nine.] Avec qui habite-t-elle ? [Who does she live with?] Elle habite avec sa mère, son père et son chat. Change je to elle and ma to sa when you copy.

Step 5, Fix common errors. A child writes Nora habite à Paris without checking the text. Correction: Nora habite à Lyon, so always find the proof. Another says Elle joue au tennis le lundi. Correction: le mercredi. A third writes Je habite; say J'habite.

Step 6, Your turn: read Hugo a dix ans. Il habite à Marseille avec sa sœur. Le samedi, il joue au football. Answer the question Que fait Hugo le samedi ? Answer: Il joue au football le samedi. [He plays football on Saturdays.]

modules.title: Writing short texts
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Writing short texts', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: write about me. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Writing short texts' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: write about me, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Texte: 'Une eleve habite a Lyon. Elle a douze ans. Elle aime lire.' Ou habite l'eleve? A Lyon. A toi d'ecrire: 'Je m'appelle... J'habite a... J'aime...' Method: Model run for 'Writing short texts'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Write about me: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Start with a sentence frame. Je m'appelle Samir. J'ai neuf ans. J'habite dans une grande ville. [My name is Samir. I am nine. I live in a big city.] Copy the frame and put your own name, age and place in it. Begin each sentence with a capital letter and end with a full stop.

Step 2, Add family and pets. J'ai un frère et une sœur. [I have a brother and a sister.] J'ai un chien. Il s'appelle Max. [I have a dog. His name is Max.] Use J'ai, not Je suis, for age, brothers, sisters and pets. Write two sentences about your own family.

Step 3, Say what you like. J'aime le football et j'aime lire. [I like football and I like reading.] Je n'aime pas les araignées. [I do not like spiders.] Join ideas with et [and] and mais [but]: J'aime la pizza, mais je n'aime pas le poisson. [I like pizza, but I do not like fish.]

Step 4, Put the text together and check it. Write six sentences in order: name, age, town, family, pet, likes. Check capitals, full stops and accents such as école, frère and très. Read it aloud once and listen for a sentence that sounds wrong.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child writes Je suis neuf ans. Correction: J'ai neuf ans. Another writes mon sœur. Correction: ma sœur, because sœur is feminine. Another writes frere without the accent. Correction: frère, with the grave accent.

Step 6, Your turn: write four sentences about you with name, age, one like and one pet. Model answer: Je m'appelle Lina. J'ai dix ans. J'aime dessiner. J'ai un chat et il s'appelle Mimi. [My name is Lina. I am ten. I like drawing. I have a cat and his name is Mimi.]

modules.title: Listening practice
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Listening practice', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: follow a short dialogue. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Listening practice' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: follow a short dialogue, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Ecoute: 'Le train part a huit heures quinze du quai trois.' Note: 8 h 15, quai 3. A dire: 'Bonjour, je m'appelle ... Je vais parler de ma ville.' Method: Model run for 'Listening practice'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Follow a short dialogue: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Prepare before listening. An adult reads the dialogue aloud twice (script in Step 2). Predict first: the title is À la boulangerie [At the bakery]. Which words might you hear? Likely pain [bread], croissant, s'il vous plaît [please], euro and some numbers. Write them down.

Step 2, Listen once for the gist. Read aloud: Bonjour, madame. Je voudrais deux croissants et une baguette, s'il vous plaît. Voilà. Un croissant coûte un euro vingt et la baguette un euro. Ça fait combien ? Trois euros quarante. Merci, au revoir ! [Hello. I would like two croissants and a baguette, please. Here you are. A croissant costs 1.20 and the baguette 1.00. How much is that? 3.40. Thank you, goodbye!] Gist: buying bread.

Step 3, Listen again for details. Note: deux croissants [2], une baguette [1], un euro vingt [1.20 each], un euro [1.00 for the baguette]. Write the numbers as figures, not words. Stop the reader after each price if you need more time.

Step 4, Check the answer by calculating. 2 x 1.20 = 2.40 and 2.40 + 1.00 = 3.40. The shopkeeper said trois euros quarante, so what you heard matches your sum. If it does not match, listen again for the number you missed.

Step 5, Fix common listening slips. Deux [2] and dix [10] sound different: deux ends with an open sound, dix with an s sound. Un euro vingt means 1.20, not 20 euros. Quarante [40] and quatorze [14] begin alike, so listen to the end of the word.
Step 6, Your turn: hear Je voudrais trois pommes. Une pomme coûte soixante centimes. Ça fait combien ? Answer: 3 x 0.60 = 1.80, so Ça fait un euro quatre-vingts. [That makes 1.80.]

modules.title: Speaking practice
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Speaking practice', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: give a short talk. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Speaking practice' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: give a short talk, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Ecoute: 'Le train part a huit heures quinze du quai trois.' Note: 8 h 15, quai 3. A dire: 'Bonjour, je m'appelle ... Je vais parler de ma ville.' Method: Model run for 'Speaking practice'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Give a short talk: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Choose a simple topic and plan four points. Topic: mon chat [my cat]. Points: name, looks, likes, how I feel. Write one keyword for each point on a small card: nom, petit et noir, dormir, je l'aime. The card helps you remember without reading every word.

Step 2, Build one sentence per point. Il s'appelle Pixel. [His name is Pixel.] Il est petit et noir. [He is small and black.] Il aime dormir et jouer avec une balle. [He likes sleeping and playing with a ball.] Je l'aime beaucoup. [I love him very much.]

Step 3, Add a start and an end. Start: Bonjour ! Je vais parler de mon chat. [Hello! I am going to talk about my cat.] End: Merci de m'écouter ! [Thank you for listening!] Your whole talk is now seven short sentences, about 30 words.

Step 4, Practise the sounds. Say each sentence slowly. The s at the end of petits is silent. In beaucoup say bo-koo. Say the talk three times: once to a mirror, once to a toy, once to a friend. Speak loudly, slowly and look up at the end of each sentence.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Il s'appelle est Pixel. Correction: Il s'appelle Pixel. Another says Il a petit. Correction: Il est petit, because we use est with an adjective. A third says Il a aime jouer. Correction: Il aime jouer, with only one verb.

Step 6, Your turn: give a five-sentence talk about your family. Model answer: Bonjour ! Je vais parler de ma famille. J'ai une sœur et un frère. Ma sœur s'appelle Rima et mon frère s'appelle Adam. Merci de m'écouter ! [Hello! I am going to talk about my family. I have a sister and a brother. My sister is Rima and my brother is Adam. Thank you for listening!]

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
